questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to keep your New Year's resolutions
The best sports for staying fit and healthy
The least exercise you need to stay healthy
Why running every day is bad for your body
questions.why: Neil says they'll ask what's the least amount of exercise someone can get away with while staying healthy.

questions.q: Why doesn't Neil keep his resolution to exercise more?
options: He is too lazy to run on cold mornings
He hurt his leg playing football
He doesn't have time after work
He doesn't like gyms or other people
questions.why: He says he's too lazy to go running on cold winter mornings and would rather stay in bed.

questions.q: Why did the UK government downgrade its exercise advice?
options: Doctors said it was too much
New research showed exercise was less important
It wanted people to rest more
Very few people were following it
questions.why: Neil says it downgraded its recommendations because so few Brits were following them.

questions.q: What is James Gallagher's regular 'structured exercise'?
options: Running on a treadmill every day
Swimming once a week
A weekly fitness class
Cycling to work
questions.why: He says his structured exercise is going for a swim once a week.

questions.q: According to Dr Zoe Saynor, what must shorter exercise sessions be like?
options: More intense
More relaxing
Done with friends
Done early in the morning
questions.why: She says shorter sessions need to be of a higher intensity.

questions.q: Why does Zoe focus on office workers?
options: They eat too much
They work very long hours
They sit down all day
They often travel by plane
questions.why: She says people with office jobs are sat down all day, so they need some easy wins.

questions.q: Which of these is an 'easy win' Zoe suggests?
options: Joining an expensive gym
Running a marathon
Swimming every day
Parking a little further away
questions.why: She mentions active travel, even parking a little bit further away.

questions.q: What does Neil say at the end about exercise?
options: He will never exercise again after this
He'll walk more, but bodies need rest
He plans to run every day from now on
He thinks walking is useless for health
questions.why: He says he'll try to walk more, 'but remember, Sam, the body needs rest too!'
